materials.name: Hill Giant Blood
materials.desc: Thick, muddy-red blood that smells of turned earth and stale ale. The humblest reagent for potions and belts of giant strength.

materials.name: Hill Giant Club-Iron
materials.desc: Crude iron bands hammered around a tree-trunk club, dented by years of brute swings. Smiths reforge it into heavy bludgeon heads.

materials.name: Hill Giant Sack-Hoard
materials.desc: A reeking hide sack stuffed with whatever caught a hill giant's eye: cart wheels, a goat skull, shiny pots, the odd coin.

materials.name: Hill Giant Essence
materials.desc: A slow, heavy glow like a sunset seen through dust. Keystone for charms that lend raw, unrefined might.

materials.name: Stone Giant Blood
materials.desc: Grey, gritty blood that settles into a fine sediment of stone dust in the vial. Brewers prize it for draughts of stone giant strength.

materials.name: Stone Giant Heartstone
materials.desc: A smooth, dream-carved throwing stone each stone giant keeps for life, polished by a lifetime of handling and faintly warm. The ideal core for a magical stone maul or earthen talisman.

materials.name: Stone Giant Boulder Shard
materials.desc: A dense wedge of granite split from a hurled boulder, still marked with the giant's grip. Masons shape it into maul heads and sling stones that hit like hammers.

materials.name: Stone Giant Essence
materials.desc: A quiet, grey luminescence that feels like the pressure deep under a mountain. Keystone for stoneskin, earth-shaping and giant-strength enchantments.

materials.name: Frost Giant Blood
materials.desc: Pale blue blood that forms a crust of rime on the inside of the vial and never quite thaws. Used for potions and belts of frost giant strength.

materials.name: Frost Giant Glacial Ice
materials.desc: Blue-black ice chipped from the glacial plates frost giants lash to their gear. It melts only slowly even in summer and chills any blade set in it.

materials.name: Frost Giant Braid
materials.desc: A rope-thick braid of frost-white hair, knotted with iron rings and trophies. Weavers twist it into cords that shrug off killing cold.

materials.name: Frost Giant Rime-Iron
materials.desc: Blackened iron from a frost giant's greataxe, forever beaded with frost. Smiths favour it for cold-touched weapons.

materials.name: Frost Giant Essence
materials.desc: A howling, ice-blue light that fogs the vessel's glass from within. Keystone for cold resistance and frost-strength enchantments.

materials.name: Fire Giant Blood
materials.desc: Magma-hot blood that glows orange and hisses when it touches steel; it must be caught in stone or crystal. The reagent for potions and belts of fire giant strength.

materials.name: Fire Giant Forge-Ash
materials.desc: Fine black ash scraped from a fire giant's apron and soot-pouch, still warm to the touch. Alchemists fold it into fire-proofing salves and tempering baths.

materials.name: Fire Giant Forge-Iron
materials.desc: Dense, ember-red iron from the forge hammer a fire giant carries, soaked in centuries of heat. Fire-aspected weapons forged from it never quite cool.

materials.name: Fire Giant Cinder-Braid
materials.desc: A braid of coarse flame-red hair studded with iron beads, smouldering at the tips without burning away. Woven into fire-resistant cloaks and cords.

materials.name: Fire Giant Essence
materials.desc: A roaring forge-glow that makes the vessel too hot to hold bare-handed. Keystone for fire resistance, flaming weapons and fire giant might.

materials.name: Cloud Giant Blood
materials.desc: Silvery, almost weightless blood that beads upward against the stopper. Few alchemists ever see it; it is the heart of potions of cloud giant strength.

materials.name: Cloudstuff
materials.desc: Solid-seeming cloud from a cloud giant's castle-hem, cool and springy as fleece. Weavers bind it into levitating cloth, but it evaporates if left unsealed.

materials.name: Sky-Silver
materials.desc: Pale, feather-light silver jewellery worn by cloud giant nobles, so light it drifts when dropped. Jewellers use it for rings and brooches of feather falling and flight.

materials.name: Cloud Giant Essence
materials.desc: A drifting, pearl-grey mist that rearranges itself into shapes when watched. Keystone for flight, fog and illusion magic.

materials.name: Storm Giant Blood
materials.desc: Blue-violet blood that crackles with tiny sparks and smells of ozone and brine. The rarest giant blood, sought for potions and belts of storm giant strength.

materials.name: Sea-Storm Pearl
materials.desc: A fist-sized, storm-grey pearl that storm giants wear as a talisman; lightning flickers deep inside it. A keystone for storm-calling and weather-command items.

materials.name: Lightning-Veined Hair
materials.desc: Long hair with bright veins that spark when brushed. Twisted into cords, it conducts and stores lightning.

materials.name: Storm Giant Essence
materials.desc: A churning thunderhead in miniature, flashing and rumbling inside the vessel. Keystone for lightning, thunder, water-breathing and control-weather enchantments.

materials.name: Ettin Blood
materials.desc: Dark, clotting blood that separates into two layers in the vial, as if it can't agree with itself. A crude substitute for hill giant blood.

materials.name: Ettin Wakeful Eye
materials.desc: One eye of an ettin's ever-watching head, bloodshot and never quite closed. Alchemists grind it into tonics against sleep and surprise.

materials.name: Ettin Morningstar Iron
materials.desc: Spiked iron balls from an ettin's twin weapons, crude but massive. Good heavy scrap for smiths.

materials.name: Ogre Blood
materials.desc: Sour, brownish blood with a faint strength-giving kick. Hedge alchemists use it for cheap brawn tonics.

materials.name: Ogre Greatclub Knot
materials.desc: The iron-hard, gnarled head of an ogre's club, stained darker than anyone likes to ask about. Solid stock for mauls and cudgels.

materials.name: Ogre Trophy Sack
materials.desc: A greasy sack of stolen oddments: a helm, a few coins, a child's doll, half a ham.

materials.name: Oni Horn
materials.desc: A lacquer-dark horn that shifts subtly in shape if you look away. Carvers turn it into masks and wands of disguise.

materials.name: Oni Blood
materials.desc: Inky blue blood that crawls back together when spilled. A potent, unwholesome ingredient in regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Oni Glaive Edge
materials.desc: The curved, wickedly keen blade of an oni's glaive, cold with fiendish menace. Reforged into cruel polearms.

materials.name: Oni Essence
materials.desc: A shifting blue-black smoke that shows a different face every time you look. Keystone for invisibility, disguise and shapechanging magic.

materials.name: Troll Blood
materials.desc: Green-black blood that keeps trying to clot into new flesh. The classic base for regenerative salves; it spoils instantly near fire or acid.

materials.name: Troll Hide
materials.desc: Rubbery, warty green hide that slowly regrows where it is cut. Tanners must sear the edges or it will seal every stitch shut.

materials.name: Troll Claw
materials.desc: A black, hooked claw that keeps growing for weeks after removal. Useful for cheap weapon spikes that repair their own chips.

materials.name: Troll Heart
materials.desc: A heart that keeps beating sluggishly in a jar, and will try to grow a new troll if left in the dark. Keystone for regeneration rings and potions of healing.

materials.name: Stone Giant Dream-Carving
materials.desc: A slab of slate carved in a trance, its flowing lines said to record what the giant saw in the waking dream of the surface. Seers use it for divination and dreamwork.

materials.name: Frost Giant's Mammoth Cloak
materials.desc: A shaggy cloak of mammoth or yeti fur big enough to roof a hut. Cut down, it makes a dozen warm cloaks.

materials.name: Fire Giant Blade Shard
materials.desc: A slab of a fire giant's greatsword, blackened steel with a glowing temper line. Reforged into flame-touched blades.

materials.name: Storm Giant Oracle Shell
materials.desc: A spiralled sea-shell storm giants listen to for omens; held to the ear, it murmurs of coming weather. A focus for divination and weather-reading.

materials.name: Ogre Hide Wraps
materials.desc: Crudely stitched hides of whatever the ogre last ate, cinched with rope. Tough, if you can bear the smell.

materials.name: Scrap Steel
materials.desc: Notched blades, bent buckles and broken helm bands. Every smith will take it by the pound.

materials.name: Scrap Leather
materials.desc: Scuffed straps, belts and armour panels still good for patching.

materials.name: Tattered Cloth
materials.desc: Stained tunics, cloaks and bandages, fit only for rags or padding.

materials.name: Scrap Chain Links
materials.desc: Handfuls of riveted rings from torn mail, useful for repairs.

materials.name: Salvaged Arrowheads
materials.desc: Iron points pulled from quivers and targets, most still sharp.

materials.name: Battered Shield Planks
materials.desc: Split boards from a shield, bound with warped iron.

materials.name: Worn Rope Coil
materials.desc: Frayed hemp rope, a few dozen feet of it, still holds a knot.

materials.name: Coin Purse
materials.desc: A pouch of mixed coin and small valuables; contents vary by owner (listed value is a rough average).

materials.name: Commoner's Sundries
materials.desc: A clay pipe, a whittling knife, a copper or two and a heel of bread.

materials.name: Watch Insignia
materials.desc: A stamped brass badge of a city watch. Useful for forgers and disguises.

materials.name: Knuckle-Duster
materials.desc: Brass knuckles worn smooth by use.

materials.name: Bone Spearhead
materials.desc: A spearhead knapped from beast bone and lashed with sinew.

materials.name: Lizardfolk Bone Club
materials.desc: A heavy club of fused bone, studded with teeth from lizardfolk kills.

materials.name: Grimlock Spiked Club
materials.desc: A club of bone set with jagged stone spikes, shaped entirely by touch.

materials.name: Goblin Scrap-Trinkets
materials.desc: Shiny junk: bottle caps, a cracked mirror, a lucky rat skull on a string.

materials.name: Holy Symbol Fragment
materials.desc: A worn amulet or broken emblem of a god, still faintly warm with devotion. Used as a focus in blessing and warding crafts.

materials.name: Acolyte's Prayer Beads
materials.desc: A string of wooden beads rubbed smooth by countless prayers.

materials.name: Blessed Holy Water
materials.desc: A flask of water consecrated by a priest, cool and clear. A binding agent for holy crafts.

materials.name: Reliquary Relic
materials.desc: A saint's knucklebone or scrap of vestment sealed in a silver case, humming with quiet grace. A strong focus for healing and protection items.

materials.name: Spellbook Pages
materials.desc: Loose pages of arcane notation, some still legible. Scribes mine them for inks and formulae.

materials.name: Arcane Focus Shard
materials.desc: A chip of a crystal orb or wand tip that still gathers a trickle of power.

materials.name: Spell Component Pouch
materials.desc: A belt pouch of compartments stuffed with bat guano, sulfur, powdered iron and stranger things.

materials.name: Mage's Spellbook Folio
materials.desc: A bound section of a working wizard's spellbook, with several mid-level spells intact.

materials.name: Archmage's Annotated Folio
materials.desc: A dense folio covered in margin notes, counter-theories and warded pages. Invaluable to scribes of powerful scrolls and tomes.

materials.name: Archmage's Focus
materials.desc: A staff-crowning crystal or rune-carved orb, attuned for decades to a master's will. It still wards against hostile magic.

materials.name: Druidic Mistletoe
materials.desc: A sprig of mistletoe cut by golden sickle and bound with bark twine. Still green long after cutting.

materials.name: Living-Wood Focus
materials.desc: A staff or totem of wood that still puts out leaves in spring. Used for growth and nature-bond items.

materials.name: Cult Idol
materials.desc: A crude, disturbing idol of a forbidden power. Unsettling to hold; useful for curses and dark rites.

materials.name: Ritual Dagger
materials.desc: A black-handled knife etched with sigils and stained from use in rites.

materials.name: Dark Pact Page
materials.desc: A page of a pact tome written in something that isn't ink, bearing a signature that twitches. Keystone fodder for curses and fiendish scrolls.

materials.name: Noble Signet
materials.desc: A gold signet ring with a house crest. Worth more to forgers or the family than to jewellers.

materials.name: Fine Silk Scraps
materials.desc: Embroidered silk and lace from courtly clothes, perfumed and bright.

materials.name: Thieves' Picks
materials.desc: A roll of lockpicks, tension wires and a tiny mirror.

materials.name: Cipher Notes
materials.desc: Coded notes and a cipher key sewn into a coat lining.

materials.name: Spyglass Lens
materials.desc: A ground lens from a scout's spyglass, flawless and clear.

materials.name: Trail Map
materials.desc: A hand-drawn map of local trails, springs and ambush points.

materials.name: Bandit Hideout Map
materials.desc: A crumpled map marking caches, lookouts and a hideout or two.

materials.name: Assassin's Poison Residue
materials.desc: Crusted vials and a stained applicator from a professional poisoner's kit. Poisoners can reconstitute a dose or two.

materials.name: Garrote Wire
materials.desc: A thin, blackened wire between two wooden grips. Silent, and very final.

materials.name: Berserker Trophy Necklace
materials.desc: Beast fangs and a few less comfortable trophies strung on sinew.

materials.name: Champion's Shield Boss
materials.desc: A polished steel boss from an arena shield, dented by many crowd-pleasing blocks.

materials.name: Campaign Medal
materials.desc: A tarnished medal from a long-past war. Soldiers regard them as lucky.

materials.name: Heraldic Plate
materials.desc: Pieces of fine plate enamelled with a knight's heraldry. A smith can rework it into quality armour.

materials.name: Scale-Studded Armour Scraps
materials.desc: Armour panels studded with shed red scales and heat-blackened rivets, never scorched by flame. Armourers use it for fire-resistant work.

materials.name: Kobold Trap Springs
materials.desc: Tightly wound springs, tripwires and hooks from kobold snares.

materials.name: Kobold Dragon Idol
materials.desc: A lovingly carved little dragon idol, blackened by offerings.

materials.name: Hobgoblin Military Kit
materials.desc: Well-kept armour, a whetstone and regimented gear stamped with a legion mark.

materials.name: Hobgoblin War Banner
materials.desc: A disciplined legion's standard; seeing it lost unnerves its soldiers.

materials.name: Bugbear Ambush Sack
materials.desc: A huge, muffled sack for bagging victims silently. Good lining for quiet cloaks.

materials.name: Gnoll Bone Fetish
materials.desc: A charm of gnawed bones and hyena teeth, dedicated to a demon of slaughter.

materials.name: Orc War Totem
materials.desc: A totem of beast skulls and red-daubed wood, carried to honour a war god.

materials.name: Shark-Tooth Trident Tip
materials.desc: A trident head barbed with rows of shark teeth. Hard to pull out of anything.

materials.name: Shark-Call Shell
materials.desc: A spiral shell sahuagin priestesses use to call their sharks; its hum carries far underwater.

materials.name: Merfolk Coral Charm
materials.desc: A bright coral pendant on kelp cord, worn for safe tides.

materials.name: Duergar Ironforged Plate
materials.desc: Dark, heavy armour plates forged in the deep with grim precision.

materials.name: Stone-Camouflage Cloak Scrap
materials.desc: A patch of mottled grey cloth that blends into rock. Weavers use it in cloaks for hiding underground.

materials.name: Deep Gnome Gem Pouch
materials.desc: A small pouch of rough-cut gems a svirfneblin was saving to trade.

materials.name: Werewolf Blood
materials.desc: Iron-dark blood that turns briefly silver in moonlight, carrying the wolf's curse. Alchemists use it (carefully) for shapechanging and regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Moon-Touched Werewolf Claw
materials.desc: A hooked grey claw that stays wolfish when the body reverts. Faintly silvered under moonlight; carved into talismans of the hunt.

materials.name: Wererat Blood
materials.desc: Thin, fast-clotting blood that smells of sewers and carries the rat's curse. Alchemists use it (carefully) for shapechanging and regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Moon-Touched Wererat Incisor
materials.desc: A long yellow incisor shed during the final reversion. Thieves wear them as charms for slipping through tight places.

materials.name: Wereboar Blood
materials.desc: Hot, heavy blood that foams when shaken, carrying the boar's curse. Alchemists use it (carefully) for shapechanging and regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Moon-Touched Wereboar Tusk
materials.desc: A curved, ivory tusk left behind when the boar-form fades. Prized for stubborn, relentless charms.

materials.name: Weretiger Blood
materials.desc: Rich, amber-tinted blood that carries the tiger's curse. Alchemists use it (carefully) for shapechanging and regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Moon-Touched Weretiger Claw
materials.desc: A sickle-curved, striped-sheath claw shed in the moment of reversion. Used in charms of grace and ambush.

materials.name: Werebear Blood
materials.desc: Dark, slow blood that carries the bear's curse, gentler than most but no less binding. Alchemists use it (carefully) for shapechanging and regenerative draughts.

materials.name: Moon-Touched Werebear Claw
materials.desc: A broad, blunt claw shed as the bear-form falls away. Druids treasure them for charms of protective strength.

monsters.name: Hill Giant
monsters.blurb: A gluttonous brute who carries a club and a sack of stolen oddities; its blood is the humblest giant-strength reagent.

harvest.note: Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Pry the bands off the club; they are riveted with giant-sized nails.
Mostly junk; roll on your DM's trinket table for anything worth keeping.
It escapes with the last breath: hold an Essence Vessel ready and stopper it within a minute.

monsters.name: Stone Giant
monsters.blurb: A reclusive, artistic giant of the deep crags whose lifelong throwing stone and gritty blood are earth-magic treasures.

harvest.note: Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Kept in a belt pouch or bound in the giant's hair. Fail by 5+ and you chip its dream-carvings, halving its value. Other stone giants may track down whoever carries it.
Gather from boulders the giant threw; a successful check finds shards with a clean grain.
Usually kept in the giant's lair rather than carried; too heavy for one person (200 lb).
A faint shimmer over the body marks it. Catch it in an Essence Vessel within a minute.

monsters.name: Frost Giant
monsters.blurb: A reaver of the frozen north whose rime-crusted blood, trophy braids and ice-bound gear all hold the bite of winter.

harvest.note: Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Chip it from armour plates and packs; it must be packed in snow to last beyond a week.
Cut at the root; the rings and trophies woven in are worth a few gp to collectors.
The axe head is too big to carry whole; it must be broken down cold, or it shatters.
A faint shimmer over the body marks it. Catch it in an Essence Vessel within a minute.

monsters.name: Fire Giant
monsters.blurb: A master smith of volcanic halls whose molten blood, forge-iron and cinder braids carry living flame.

harvest.note: Too hot for glass: catch it in a stone or crystal vial within the hour. Without fire resistance or heavy gloves you take 1d6 fire damage.
Scraped from its apron and soot-pouches.
The hammer must be broken down at a forge; carrying it whole needs a cart.
Still smoulders when cut; douse it in sand, not water, or it cracks.
Let the blade cool an hour before breaking it down, or it scorches your tools.
It escapes with the last breath: hold an Essence Vessel ready and stopper it within a minute.

monsters.name: Cloud Giant
monsters.blurb: A proud, gambling sky-noble whose silvery blood, sky-silver finery and cloudstuff hem are the stuff of flight magic.

harvest.note: The blood drifts upward as it leaves the wound; catch it from above, or it floats away. Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Gather it into a sealed jar before it disperses; unsealed it thins to mist in a week.
Rings, torcs and brooches; weigh them down, as they tend to drift off in a breeze.
Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute of death, or it's gone.

monsters.name: Storm Giant
monsters.blurb: A solitary oracle-king of the sea and sky whose ozone-sharp blood, storm pearls and lightning-veined hair are among the rarest giant relics.

harvest.note: Each vial sparks as it fills; touching the blood bare-handed deals 1d6 lightning damage. Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Worn as a talisman or set in a crown; not every storm giant carries one (DM's choice).
Cut with a non-metal blade, or each stroke discharges a painful shock.
Found in its sea-lair or satchel; it goes silent if cracked.
It escapes with the last breath: hold an Essence Vessel ready and stopper it within a minute.

monsters.name: Ettin
monsters.blurb: A bickering two-headed brute, one head always awake; its eyes are a folk remedy against sleep.

harvest.note: Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Only the head that was 'on watch' at death yields a usable eye; the other is dull and useless.

monsters.name: Ogre
monsters.blurb: A dim, hungry bully with more muscle than sense; it yields cheap brawn tonics and a club that could stop a door.

harvest.note: Draw it from a major vein within the hour into stoppered vials; a giant yields enough for one vial of reagent-grade blood.
Hold your nose; there is usually 2d6 sp at the bottom.

monsters.name: Oni
monsters.blurb: A fiendish ogre-mage that wears stolen faces and turns invisible; its horns and self-mending blood are prized by illusionists and healers.

harvest.note: Saw at the base while the body is still warm; once cold the horn hardens like iron (+2 DC).
Stir with silver while collecting, or the blood crawls back into the corpse.
Seal it in an Essence Vessel within a minute of death, or it's gone.

monsters.name: Troll
monsters.blurb: A ravenous regenerator that only fire or acid will finish; everything taken from it tries to heal.

harvest.note: Must be kept well away from fire and acid: a single spark curdles it to worthless sludge.
Only possible once the troll is dead by fire or acid; sear each cut edge or it knits back together.
Fail by 5+ and the heart squirms free and must be recaptured (DC 12 Dexterity). Store in a lightless jar and feed it nothing.

monsters.name: Werewolf
monsters.blurb: A cursed hunter who reverts to human form in death, leaving curse-laden blood and a single claw that never changed back.

harvest.note: Wear gloves: fail the check by 5+ bare-handed and you risk contracting the lycanthropy (DC 12 Constitution save). Silver implements keep the blood from clotting; it is most potent collected under moonlight.
Only this one beast-part keeps its shape when the body reverts; search within the hour, before the moonlight fades from it.
They were people too; their belongings deserve respect, or at least a proper burial.

monsters.name: Wererat
monsters.blurb: A cursed schemer of the sewers whose blood carries the rat's curse and whose last shed tooth is a thief's charm.

harvest.note: Wear gloves: fail the check by 5+ bare-handed and you risk contracting the lycanthropy (DC 12 Constitution save). Silver implements keep the blood from clotting; it is most potent collected under moonlight.
Only this one beast-part keeps its shape when the body reverts; search within the hour, before the moonlight fades from it.
They were people too; their belongings deserve respect, or at least a proper burial.

monsters.name: Wereboar
monsters.blurb: A cursed, short-tempered brute whose blood and shed tusk carry the boar's stubborn rage.

harvest.note: Wear gloves: fail the check by 5+ bare-handed and you risk contracting the lycanthropy (DC 12 Constitution save). Silver implements keep the blood from clotting; it is most potent collected under moonlight.
Only this one beast-part keeps its shape when the body reverts; search within the hour, before the moonlight fades from it.
They were people too; their belongings deserve respect, or at least a proper burial.

monsters.name: Weretiger
monsters.blurb: A proud, solitary cursed hunter whose blood and final shed claw carry feline grace.

harvest.note: Wear gloves: fail the check by 5+ bare-handed and you risk contracting the lycanthropy (DC 12 Constitution save). Silver implements keep the blood from clotting; it is most potent collected under moonlight.
Only this one beast-part keeps its shape when the body reverts; search within the hour, before the moonlight fades from it.
They were people too; their belongings deserve respect, or at least a proper burial.

monsters.name: Werebear
monsters.blurb: A reclusive, often good-hearted cursed guardian whose blood and shed claw carry protective strength.

harvest.note: Wear gloves: fail the check by 5+ bare-handed and you risk contracting the lycanthropy (DC 12 Constitution save). Silver implements keep the blood from clotting; it is most potent collected under moonlight.
Only this one beast-part keeps its shape when the body reverts; search within the hour, before the moonlight fades from it.
They were people too; their belongings deserve respect, or at least a proper burial.

monsters.name: Acolyte
monsters.blurb: A junior temple servant; carries little but devotions.

harvest.note: Usually only a few copper.

monsters.name: Archmage
monsters.blurb: A master of the arcane whose study-worn belongings are worth a small fortune to scribes and enchanters.

harvest.note: The folio is warded: fail by 5+ and a glyph flares, burning half the pages (value halved).
Found on its staff or in a warded pouch.

monsters.name: Assassin
monsters.blurb: A paid killer whose kit is a poisoner's treasure, and a danger to careless looters.

harvest.note: Fail by 5+ and you are nicked by a coated blade (DC 13 Constitution save or 2d6 poison damage).

monsters.name: Bandit
monsters.blurb: A cutthroat of the road; their pockets hold whatever the last victim had.

monsters.name: Bandit Captain
monsters.blurb: A bandit leader with better gear, a fatter purse and a map to the gang's caches.

monsters.name: Berserker
monsters.blurb: A raider who fights in a frenzy; their trophies are worn with pride.

monsters.name: Bugbear
monsters.blurb: A hulking goblinoid ambusher that carries a victim-sized sack and a heavy morningstar.

monsters.name: Commoner
monsters.blurb: An ordinary villager; loot them and you'll find only a life's small comforts.

monsters.name: Cult Fanatic
monsters.blurb: A zealous cult leader who carries fragments of the pact that empowers them.

harvest.note: Fail by 5+ and the page's whispered name lingers: disadvantage on your next Wisdom save within 24 hours.

monsters.name: Cultist
monsters.blurb: A robed devotee of dark powers; their trinkets are crude but tainted.

harvest.note: Not every cultist carries one; on a fail it's just a painted stone.

monsters.name: Deep Gnome (Svirfneblin)
monsters.blurb: A wary gnome of the deep roads, cloaked to vanish against stone and usually carrying gems to trade.

harvest.note: Svirfneblin hide their gems well; look inside boot heels.

monsters.name: Druid
monsters.blurb: A keeper of the wilds whose focus and herbs still hum with primal life.

harvest.note: It wilts within a day if cut or split; keep it whole.

monsters.name: Duergar
monsters.blurb: A grim dwarf of the deep who works iron like a curse; its plate is dark and dense.

monsters.name: Gladiator
monsters.blurb: An arena champion kitted out for show and slaughter alike.

monsters.name: Gnoll
monsters.blurb: A hyena-headed raider devoted to a demon of slaughter; its fetishes reek of the Abyss.

monsters.name: Goblin
monsters.blurb: A sneaky little raider with pockets full of junk and the odd genuine find.

monsters.name: Grimlock
monsters.blurb: A blind cave-dweller with keen senses and crude, touch-shaped weapons.

monsters.name: Guard
monsters.blurb: A town watchman in patched mail with a badge and a few coins.

harvest.note: Looting a watchman may draw more watchmen.

monsters.name: Half-Red Dragon Veteran
monsters.blurb: A seasoned warrior with a red dragon's blood and fiery breath, armoured in scale-studded plate that no flame has marked.

harvest.note: Only the armour; the veteran is a person, not a quarry.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin
monsters.blurb: A disciplined goblinoid legionary with well-maintained military gear.

harvest.note: Only one per unit, usually carried by the sergeant.

monsters.name: Knight
monsters.blurb: A sworn warrior in heraldic plate; plundering one invites the ire of their order.

harvest.note: Must be unbuckled piece by piece; hacking it off ruins the enamel (value halved).
Only knights of noble birth.

monsters.name: Kobold
monsters.blurb: A small, trap-loving dragon-worshipper; its snares are worth more than its purse.

harvest.note: Kobolds guard these fiercely; one per warren.

monsters.name: Lizardfolk
monsters.blurb: A pragmatic reptilian hunter armed with bone clubs and hide shields.

monsters.name: Mage
monsters.blurb: A capable wizard whose component pouch and spellbook are the real prize.

harvest.note: Fail by 5+ and a protective rune erases the best spell.

monsters.name: Merfolk
monsters.blurb: A sea-dweller with coral charms and a spear; little else survives the tides.

monsters.name: Noble
monsters.blurb: A pampered aristocrat dripping in finery and entitlement.

monsters.name: Orc
monsters.blurb: A fierce raider devoted to a war god; its totems and heavy weapons are crude but sturdy.

harvest.note: Carried by one warrior in five.

monsters.name: Priest
monsters.blurb: An ordained cleric carrying blessed water and a sacred relic.

harvest.note: Looting a relic from a temple priest is sacrilege to their faith; expect consequences.

monsters.name: Sahuagin
monsters.blurb: A shark-toothed raider of the deep whose tridents and calling shells are cruelly practical.

harvest.note: Carried by priestesses and chieftains.

monsters.name: Scout
monsters.blurb: A keen-eyed ranger with a spyglass and hand-drawn maps.

monsters.name: Spy
monsters.blurb: A professional informant with picks, ciphers and secrets sewn into their clothes.

harvest.note: Hidden in a coat lining; fail and you miss it entirely.

monsters.name: Thug
monsters.blurb: A hired bruiser with brass knuckles and a heavy cudgel.

monsters.name: Tribal Warrior
monsters.blurb: A hunter-warrior of a wilderness people, armed with hand-made bone and hide gear.

monsters.name: Veteran
monsters.blurb: A grizzled soldier with well-kept arms and a medal or two.
